new_primary_readings.title: Achieving Full-View Coverage in Camera Sensor Networks
new_primary_readings.publication: ACM Transactions on Sensor Networks 10(1), Article 3; November 2013 from PDF page footer
new_primary_readings.source_level: primary author-hosted PDF copied earlier by R1_atlas; original-byte hash checked here
new_primary_readings.reading_scope: Sections 2, 3.1, 3.2; Lemmas 3.1–3.3, Theorem 3.4; Section4.1 and Lemmas4.1–4.3 proof text. Figures referred by text; no new rendering here. Remaining pages not read.
classification: angular gap and regional boundary verification
new_primary_readings.original_problem: Given fixed directional camera sectors, certify every target facing orientation within effective angle theta<pi/2; random sensor density estimation additionally assumes boundary treatment and uniform deployment.
new_primary_readings.mechanism: Maximum gap of circularly ordered viewing vectors <=2theta; partition into constant covering-sensor subregions, then validate continuously along segmented boundaries; grid-to-continuum needs explicit radius/angular margins.
new_primary_readings.task_transfer: Treat each genuinely measured point for a channel as a receiver location. Certify the 1000m eligible receivers surround each possible source. At theta=pi/2 prove separately using closed halfplanes/convex hull; do not reuse singular safe-arc formulas. Use per-leaf witness masks to test station deletion.
new_primary_readings.implementation: Completed optimistic full-trajectory 12-case diagnostic. 252 individual station-case checks: 2 exact continuous certificates, 96 exact separation witnesses, 154 undecided. Not deployed; unknown-channel costs/timing remain.
new_primary_readings.benchmark_results: Not transferred; evaluation section not read this turn.
new_primary_readings.limitations: No theorem here says extra measurements shorten online robot paths. Unknown channels have not been measured at localization stops; they cannot obtain free coverage. Added sensing must be paid and compared. Theta endpoint, finite disk boundary, variable radius and mixed sources need task-specific proof.

new_primary_readings.title: Near Optimal Bayesian Active Learning for Decision Making
new_primary_readings.source_level: Primary original PDF cached and extracted by R1_atlas; read page text here
new_primary_readings.reading_scope: Problem assumptions and overlapping action regions; HEC splitting multisets and expected cut mass; robotic results/limitations. Theoretical proof pages 5–7 not read here.
new_primary_readings.original_model: Known prior over finite hypotheses, deterministic finite test outcomes, unit or fixed nonuniform test costs; every surviving hypothesis must lie in one successful decision region.
new_primary_readings.task_transfer: One-step paid supplemental bearing scored by predicted continuation action cost and Q4 visibility. Keep true continuous region as sole certificate. No-signal cannot imply outside a radius-1000 disk for Q4.
new_primary_readings.implementation: Future proposed Q4 study; not attributed to earlier R3 R5 registration. R2 own Q3 proxy is an implementation reference, not the HEC algorithm.
new_primary_readings.limitations: No HEC hypergraph implementation or adaptive-submodular/approximation guarantee is claimed. Q4 uncertain direction and fixed spatial noise violate original finite deterministic assumptions; any expectation is a local assumed planning proxy.
new_primary_readings.benchmark_results: No paper performance values transferred. Paper says short robot horizons allow myopic VoI performance close to HEC; not a task benchmark for this contest.
